title: fix(ios): pasting an image into the chat composer does nothing
body: Closes #161626 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where iOS users who copy an image and try to paste it into the chat composer get no attachment. For example, a user takes a screenshot, crops it, and taps **Copy and Delete**. Then the user long-presses the composer, and the edit menu offers no **Paste** action (only **AutoFill**). The only workaround was to save the image to Photos and attach it through the photo picker. The macOS composer already supports image paste. The iOS composer only accepted text paste. ## Why This Change Was Made The iOS composer text view now uses the same paste contract as the macOS composer (`ChatComposerNSTextView`): - It offers **Paste** when the pasteboard has images. - It stages each pasted item through the existing `onPasteImageAttachment` → `addImageAttachment` path, so size limits, JPEG transcoding, and session ownership are the same as for other image attachments. - It leaves text-only paste to UIKit. Each item uses its first representation that ImageIO can decode, because the upload transcoder uses ImageIO. For example, an item that offers SVG before PNG uses the PNG. When the composer is embedded with attachments disabled, the paste callback is nil and UIKit's default paste behavior is not changed. Non-goals, same as macOS: when one paste has both an image and text, the image wins and the text is not inserted. File URLs from the Files app are not handled. ## User Impact On iPhone and iPad, a long-press **Paste** (or hardware ⌘V) in the chat composer now attaches a copied image, such as a cropped screenshot, a photo copied from Photos, or an image copied from Safari. The image appears as a normal attachment chip that can be removed or sent. Text paste does not change. ## Evidence All runs were on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 26.5), Xcode on an Intel Mac, with this branch's exact diff applied to base `006de596042`. **1. Real app, before/after (new UI test `testChatComposerPastesClipboardImageAsAttachment`).** The test puts an image-only item on the general pasteboard. This is the same shape as a screenshot shared with Copy and Delete. Then the test long-presses the composer, taps **Paste**, and expects the attachment chip. - Stock sources (test only): fails with `XCTAssertTrue failed - PASTE_MENU_MISSING`. The edit menu shows only AutoFill. - With the fix: `Test Case '-[OpenClawUITests.OpenClawSnapshotUITests testChatComposerPastesClipboardImageAsAttachment]' passed (13.364 seconds).` | Before: long-press menu (no Paste) | After: long-press menu | After: tapped Paste | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | The chip reads `pasted-image-1.jpg` because staging transcodes the pasted PNG to JPEG. No "Allow Paste" prompt appeared during the user-initiated paste. **2. Unit test (`ChatComposerTextViewIOSTests`, run with `xcodebuild -scheme OpenClawKit-Package` on the iOS simulator):** ``` ✔ Test "pasted images become attachments and text falls through" passed ✔ Test run with 4 tests in 1 suite passed ``` This test uses a private pasteboard. It covers raw PNG data, a `UIImage` item, text only (no attachment, falls through), an item that offers SVG before PNG (uses PNG), and a nil callback (no attachment). I checked that it is not vacuous. When I replaced the ImageIO filter with `conforms(to: .image)`, it failed as expected: `(pasted.map(\.mimeType) → ["image/svg+xml"]) == ["image/png"]`. **3. Neighboring regressions:** - `ChatTypingFocusTests`: `Executed 5 tests, with 0 failures`. - UI tests `testChatComposerReturnInsertsNewlineWithoutSending` and `testCodeBlockCopyButtonCopiesRawCode`: passed. - The build's SwiftFormat and SwiftLint phases passed (`0/432 files require formatting`, `Found 0 violations`). **Not covered:** - `testChatComposerStartsCompactAndGrowsWithDraft` fails at `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.swift:429`, a model-picker assertion. It fails the same way with this PR's source changes removed, so it is not caused by this PR. - I did not test on a physical device. I did not test the Photos-app screenshot editor itself, because the simulator cannot drive it. The test reproduces the same image-only pasteboard shape. - I did not test mixed image+text pasteboards or hardware ⌘V. Both go through the same `paste(_:)` override. AI-assisted: I made and verified this change with Claude Code (Opus 5.5). I reviewed the diff and ran all the evidence above.
